html:
SMTO-BOOT-0022 — A Conda environment with that name already exists

GUID: a0f427ab-8eaa-4560-bdb9-f047274d7c74
Slug: boot-conda-environment-exists
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The installer only creates new Conda environments, and one with this name is already there. It stopped without touching the existing environment or anything installed in it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. To see whether the existing environment already works, run the installer with --verify-only before the name, for example ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh --verify-only vllm Check-only mode tests the installed vLLM and graphics card access without installing or changing anything.
  2. To make a separate new install instead, run the installer with a name that doesn't appear in conda env list, for example my-vllm. A new name leaves the existing environment exactly as it is.
  3. If an earlier install stopped partway, use a new name for the next attempt instead of the old one. A stopped attempt can leave a half-built environment under that name, and the installer won't install over it.

What success looks like

  • Check-only mode ends with "vLLM verification complete", or a new install prints "Creating environment" followed by the new name.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0022 line and the Error reference line, and send it to the person who manages your model setup. Don't delete the existing environment unless you're sure nothing else uses it; model launchers may depend on it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • install-vllm.sh (fresh-install mode) found an existing Conda environment with the requested name and exited before hardware probing, environment creation or package installation.

What this means

  • Fresh installation queries Conda and finds the requested environment already exists. Fresh installation exits before hardware planning, environment creation or package installation; the existing named environment is preserved. An existing name does not establish whether that environment contains a healthy vLLM installation.

Why this can happen

  • Fresh installation queries Conda and finds the requested environment already exists.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the existing environment before choosing verification or a new name.

How to fix it

  • Run install-vllm.sh --verify-only with that name to check the existing environment, or rerun the install with an unused name. To reuse the name for a fresh install, remove the environment deliberately (conda env remove --name followed by that name) only after confirming nothing depends on it; an existing name says nothing about whether its vLLM install is healthy.
  • Use --verify-only to inspect that environment or choose a new name for a fresh install.

Retry and execution caution

  • Run --verify-only for the existing environment, or select an unused name for a deliberate new install.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh install uses a deliberate unused name, preserving the existing environment.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Fresh installation exits before hardware planning, environment creation or package installation; the existing named environment is preserved.
  • An existing name does not establish whether that environment contains a healthy vLLM installation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
